hints.title: Common Element Index Sum Minimization
hints.text: Both people must agree on a shared restaurant that minimizes the sum of their individual preference indices.

hints.title: Index Mapping Invariant
hints.text: Storing restaurant names and their zero-based positions from the first list in a lookup structure enables constant time index lookups during list two traversal.

hints.title: Lookup Minimal Sum Filter Procedure
hints.text: Create a mapping from restaurant name to its index in list one. Initialize minimum sum to infinity and an empty result list. Iterate over list two. If a name exists in the mapping, compute total index sum. If total is less than minimum sum, reset result to this name; if equal, append it. Return result.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.notes: Optimal solution achieving O(N + M) time and O(N) auxiliary space.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing every pair of restaurants with nested loops takes quadratic O(N * M) time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Hashing list one indices enables linear O(N + M) total traversal with O(N) auxiliary memory.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate should handle ties properly by collecting all restaurants matching the lowest index sum.
